svg.aria-label: How to write 新: 13 strokes · 12 pen lifts · 13 movements
svg.title: Writing 新
svg.desc: 13 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 新 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 新.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E6%96%B0.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 新, in three pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 on the upper left: a dot, a horizontal, two short strokes, then a horizontal along its foot. Medians 6–9 draw the tree piece under it: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 10–13 draw the right side as 所 ends: a flat left-falling stroke, a long left-falling stroke that drops down, a horizontal and a long vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
